decisions.title: Normative authority and contradictory artifacts
decisions.section: Meta JSON Schema, Server Object, and Examples
decisions.issue: The prose permits relative and variable-templated server URLs while the published meta-schema rejects them, and official examples declare older feature lines.
interpretations: Treat the meta-schema as infallible.
Treat examples as implicit amendments.
Give normative prose precedence and retain every divergence as evidence.
decisions.peer_behavior: The maintained santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema validator enforces the published schema literally; official examples retain their historical versions.
decisions.selected_behavior: Normative prose controls; only the contradictory Server URL format assertion is removed, and official example versions are preserved.
decisions.rationale: Normative prose has greater authority than an informative schema or example when those artifacts conflict.
decisions.security_consequences: The narrow rewrite cannot disable unrelated structural checks.
decisions.resource_consequences: Server expressions remain parsed under finite limits and all pinned artifacts remain checksum verified.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Relative and templated server URLs remain accepted, while new feature lines require an explicit inventory.
decisions.wire_consequences: Historical example version bytes and accepted server URL forms are preserved.
decisions.upstream_status: No upstream erratum currently supersedes the pinned prose.
decisions.reconsider_when: OpenRPC publishes a corrected meta-schema, relabels the examples, or issues a precedence erratum.

decisions.title: Reference Object siblings and unknown members
decisions.issue: The Reference Object schema allows only $ref and does not define evaluation or preservation semantics for siblings.
interpretations: Ignore all siblings.
Preserve siblings without evaluating them.
Reject every sibling exactly as the published object schema requires.
decisions.peer_behavior: Reference sibling handling varies across JSON Schema and OpenAPI generations; the pinned OpenRPC schema declares only $ref.
decisions.selected_behavior: A Reference Object contains exactly one non-empty $ref, and strict typed parsing rejects every sibling including x- members.
decisions.rationale: Rejecting undefined siblings preserves the exact pinned object contract without inventing evaluation semantics.
decisions.security_consequences: Rejected siblings cannot smuggle ignored policy data beside a reference.
decisions.resource_consequences: URI-reference length and syntax remain bounded separately.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Documents relying on Reference Object siblings are rejected rather than normalized.
decisions.wire_consequences: No sibling is silently stripped or emitted.
decisions.upstream_status: No sibling extension is present in OpenRPC 1.4.1.
decisions.reconsider_when: A released OpenRPC feature line defines Reference Object sibling processing.

decisions.title: Reference resolution and cycle boundaries
decisions.section: JSON Schema Object and Reference Object
decisions.issue: OpenRPC object references and embedded JSON Schema references share URI syntax but not recursion or retrieval semantics.
interpretations: Never resolve references.
Resolve every reference with one algorithm.
Separate OpenRPC object traversal from Draft 7 schema resource compilation.
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained Draft 7 validators support recursive schemas, while general JSON Reference resolvers differ on cycles and external loading.
decisions.selected_behavior: Core parsing performs no I/O; caller-supplied stores resolve bounded OpenRPC references while recursive Draft 7 references remain schema resources.
decisions.rationale: Separating reference domains preserves valid recursive schemas and prevents implicit external access.
decisions.security_consequences: External access is disabled by default and scheme, host, redirect, IP, and cancellation policies fail closed.
decisions.resource_consequences: Fetch bytes, fan-out, depth, alias count, and total resources are bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Recursive schemas remain valid while cyclic OpenRPC object graphs fail explicitly.
decisions.wire_consequences: Resolution does not rewrite source documents unless the caller explicitly requests dereferencing or bundling.
decisions.upstream_status: OpenRPC 1.4.1 does not define a retrieval or cycle algorithm.
decisions.reconsider_when: OpenRPC standardizes resolution, bundling, cycle, or retrieval semantics.

decisions.title: Method, descriptor, and error uniqueness
decisions.section: Method Object names, parameters, and errors
decisions.issue: Draft 7 cannot express uniqueness by method name, descriptor name, or arbitrary-precision error code, especially through references.
interpretations: Validate inline elements only.
Let later entries overwrite earlier entries.
Collect deterministic diagnostics before and after bounded resolution.
decisions.peer_behavior: The official meta-schema validates shapes but cannot enforce identity constraints; generators commonly map names into registries.
decisions.selected_behavior: Validation reports duplicate methods, parameters, error codes, and invalid parameter ordering deterministically before and after resolution.
decisions.rationale: The normative uniqueness rules must not depend on map overwrite behavior or floating-point conversion.
decisions.security_consequences: Deterministic rejection prevents collision-driven registry replacement.
decisions.resource_consequences: Method, integer, and diagnostic work is bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Ambiguous documents fail instead of selecting a first or last declaration.
decisions.wire_consequences: By-position order remains observable and by-name identity is exact and case-sensitive.
decisions.upstream_status: The pinned prose contains the identity rules, while its meta-schema cannot encode them.
decisions.reconsider_when: A released specification changes identity, case sensitivity, parameter ordering, or error-code rules.

decisions.title: Example pairing validation
decisions.section: Method Object examples and Example Pairing Object
decisions.issue: OpenRPC defines no complete algorithm for asserting example values against referenced descriptors, defaults, annotations, or custom formats.
interpretations: Reject every schema-incompatible example.
Validate only easily paired inline values.
Preserve examples as documentation unless a caller explicitly asserts them.
decisions.peer_behavior: The official meta-schema and examples establish structural shapes but no value-to-schema conformance corpus.
decisions.selected_behavior: Parsing preserves example values and semantic validation checks structure and reference syntax without claiming schema assertion.
decisions.rationale: A partial implicit assertion would create inconsistent acceptance and could trigger application-specific behavior.
decisions.security_consequences: Documentation validation cannot trigger callbacks, external loading, or execution.
decisions.resource_consequences: Example JSON remains subject to parser byte, depth, value, and collection limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Schema-incompatible examples remain round-trip safe; a future assertion API must be opt-in.
decisions.wire_consequences: Explicit nulls, references, and notification result absence are preserved exactly.
decisions.upstream_status: No normative example assertion algorithm or official assertion corpus exists in the pinned release.
decisions.reconsider_when: OpenRPC defines example assertion semantics or publishes a value-validation corpus.

decisions.title: JSON Schema dialect and resource selection
decisions.issue: Schema Objects can contain arbitrary JSON, identifiers, and external references, but inferring a newer dialect would change their meaning.
interpretations: Use the newest JSON Schema dialect.
Honor any embedded $schema declaration.
Compile every OpenRPC Schema Object with Draft 7 semantics.
decisions.peer_behavior: General validators often select dialects from $schema, while OpenRPC 1.4.1 explicitly requires Draft 7.
decisions.selected_behavior: Every OpenRPC Schema Object is preserved as exact JSON and compiled with Draft 7 semantics using explicit resource maps only.
decisions.rationale: The OpenRPC dialect requirement controls instead of validator defaults or newer keywords.
decisions.security_consequences: No implicit external loader is installed.
decisions.resource_consequences: Compilation bounds resources, bytes, depth, operations, regular expressions, diagnostics, and cancellation.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Draft 7 keywords retain Draft 7 meaning across supported OpenRPC feature lines.
decisions.wire_consequences: Boolean schemas, exact numbers, identifiers, and reference lexemes are preserved.
decisions.upstream_status: Draft 7 and the OpenRPC companion meta-schema are pinned with hashes.
decisions.reconsider_when: A supported OpenRPC feature line adopts another dialect or defines dialect negotiation.

decisions.title: `rpc.discover` transport and cache semantics
decisions.section: Reserved method names and transport-independent request handling
decisions.issue: OpenRPC fixes the discovery name and result while JSON-RPC reserves rpc., but neither defines registration, filtering, caching, or invalidation.
interpretations: Register rpc.discover as an application method.
Use an implicit global registry and cache.
Provide transport-neutral lifecycle components and an explicit system-method adapter.
decisions.peer_behavior: Frameworks differ in system-method registration and dynamic description generation.
decisions.selected_behavior: The service owns validation and canonical output; the adapter uses explicit system-method registration and caching remains opt-in and explicitly invalidated.
decisions.rationale: Explicit lifecycle ownership avoids hidden global state while respecting the reserved JSON-RPC namespace.
decisions.security_consequences: Visibility filtering runs before publication and invalid documents fail closed.
decisions.resource_consequences: Provider work, output bytes, waiters, retained data, and cancellation are bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: The discovery method remains exactly rpc.discover and cache lifetime remains application owned.
decisions.wire_consequences: The result is canonical raw OpenRPC JSON encoded by normal JSON-RPC result handling.
decisions.upstream_status: Transport binding and cache semantics remain package-owned.
decisions.reconsider_when: OpenRPC standardizes discovery caching, transport binding, authorization, or revision semantics.

decisions.title: Extension members and non-standard fields
decisions.issue: Only selected objects are extensible, while unknown fields may be future members, mistakes, or data that an explicit proxy needs to preserve.
interpretations: Reject every unknown field.
Treat every unknown field as an extension.
Separate strict conformance parsing from explicit lossless preservation.
decisions.peer_behavior: Validators vary between strict rejection and forward-compatible retention; OpenRPC requires the x- extension prefix at declared extension points.
decisions.selected_behavior: Duplicate names are rejected; extensible objects accept x- fields, strict mode rejects other unknowns, and explicit preserving mode retains them without granting semantics.
decisions.rationale: Separate modes preserve strict conformance and intentional proxy workflows without conflating unknown data with extensions.
decisions.security_consequences: Duplicate rejection and collision checks prevent shadowed standard fields.
decisions.resource_consequences: All retained values remain bounded by parser limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Strict mode reports unsupported fields while preserving mode can round-trip them.
decisions.wire_consequences: Canonical output remains deterministic and exact source bytes remain available only in preserving mode.
decisions.upstream_status: Extensible object locations and field policy are pinned in the source and object-field matrix.
decisions.reconsider_when: A new OpenRPC feature line changes standard members or extension points.

decisions.title: Canonical and preserving serialization
decisions.issue: OpenRPC requires JSON but defines no canonical byte output, while deterministic discovery and lossless proxying require different profiles.
interpretations: Preserve input bytes everywhere.
Use ordinary encoder output.
Expose separate deterministic typed and exact preserving operations.
decisions.peer_behavior: Generic JSON encoders differ in whitespace, escaping, number handling, and key ordering.
decisions.selected_behavior: MarshalCanonical emits deterministic typed JSON but does not claim RFC 8785; preserving parses retain owned original bytes.
decisions.rationale: Separate explicit profiles avoid making canonicalization and lossless proxying conflicting hidden defaults.
decisions.security_consequences: Collision and malformed-value failures are explicit and no extension is executed.
decisions.resource_consequences: Canonical output is bounded and detached from caller storage.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Canonical bytes are stable for equivalent typed documents under this package version.
decisions.wire_consequences: Canonical output sorts keys and removes insignificant whitespace while preserving mode can re-emit exact accepted bytes.
decisions.reconsider_when: OpenRPC adopts a canonicalization profile or interoperability evidence requires a versioned byte contract.

decisions.title: Composition conflicts, order, and overlays
decisions.issue: OpenRPC does not define multi-document merging, collision resolution, overlay ordering, root ownership, or reference rewriting.
interpretations: Always keep the last input.
Always keep the first input.
Require an explicit bounded conflict policy and deterministic output.
decisions.peer_behavior: Generic merge tools use order-dependent overwrite or JSON Merge Patch without understanding OpenRPC identities.
decisions.selected_behavior: Merge requires equal versions, defaults to ConflictError, supports explicit KeepFirst or KeepLast, and applies bounded ordered RFC 7396 overlays.
decisions.rationale: Explicit conflict policy prevents silent contract overwrite while preserving intentional ordered composition.
decisions.security_consequences: Default collision failure prevents attacker-controlled contract replacement.
decisions.resource_consequences: Inputs, methods, components, patches, traversal, and cancellation are bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: No duplicate is selected silently and callers own any first-or-last choice.
decisions.wire_consequences: Merged registries are deterministic while overlays remain explicitly order-sensitive.
decisions.reconsider_when: OpenRPC standardizes overlays, composition, or component collision semantics.

decisions.title: Semantic diff and unresolved compatibility
decisions.issue: OpenRPC defines no API compatibility algorithm, and unresolved references or JSON Schema implication can conceal changes.
interpretations: Compare canonical bytes.
Treat every change as breaking.
Classify known structural changes and keep uncertain cases conditional.
decisions.peer_behavior: API diff tools use different compatibility models and schema approximations; no maintained peer is normative for this package.
decisions.selected_behavior: Diff classifies known changes deterministically, keeps schema and unresolved cases conditional, and fails compatibility closed on incomplete reports.
decisions.rationale: A bounded conditional result is more accurate than claiming arbitrary schema implication or optimistic compatibility.
decisions.security_consequences: Diagnostics contain bounded stable summaries rather than document payloads.
decisions.resource_consequences: Methods, components, changes, resolution, and cancellation are bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: A positive result means no breaking or conditional finding was observed in a complete bounded comparison.
decisions.wire_consequences: The comparison is read-only and does not normalize or rewrite either document.
decisions.reconsider_when: OpenRPC publishes compatibility guidance or evidence exposes a misclassified consumer break.
